title: Welcome to Cybersecurity
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate core competence across computer systems and troubleshooting.
Perform authorized hands-on work and preserve technical evidence.
Explain decisions using security, operational and risk concepts.
Produce professional documentation and complete practical assessments.
Reflect on limitations and identify the next competency to develop.

sections.heading: What is Cybersecurity?
sections.body: Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, accounts, networks, and information from damage, misuse, or unauthorised access. Think of it like securing a home: you understand what needs protection, check doors and windows, use suitable locks, and respond carefully when something seems wrong.

sections.heading: Why is it useful?
sections.body: Cybersecurity helps protect mobile-money accounts, school records, small-business information, online services, and personal devices. It also helps organisations in Kenya and across Africa reduce the risk of data loss, fraud, service disruption, and privacy breaches.

sections.heading: What can you build or do with it?
sections.body: This programme begins with computer systems, troubleshooting, operating systems, and safe technical practice before moving into more specialised security skills. You will learn to inspect systems, explain risks, carry out controlled practical tasks, and document evidence; later stages build on these foundations.

sections.heading: How to use these lessons
sections.body: Read the safety scope and explanation before touching a tool or system, predict what you expect to observe, and then perform only the authorised activity. Use the knowledge checks and practical activities to test your understanding, record evidence, and explain your decisions; stop if a task goes beyond its stated scope.

sections.heading: What you need
sections.body: No previous cybersecurity experience is required to begin, but you should be ready to follow instructions carefully and use an approved computer. Marian's isolated labs or explicitly approved virtual machines are used for practical work; internet may be needed for learning resources, but practical exercises must stay within the authorised lab environment. Cybersecurity skills are for legal, ethical and authorised use only: practise on your own devices, designated training labs, or systems for which you have clear written permission.

terms.meaning: A rule that determines what a user or process is allowed to access or change.
terms.example: A user can read but not edit a file.
terms.how_used: Operating systems use permissions to control files, devices, and other resources.
terms.when_to_use: When deciding who or what should have access to a resource.
terms.why_it_matters: Least privilege reduces the damage caused by mistakes or compromised accounts.
terms.practical_example: A lab folder is readable by learners but writable only by the lab service.
terms.example_explanation: Different permissions give each role only the access it needs.
